7.13 Local closedness, Breuil–Kisin lattice towers, and trace-limit transfer

Propositions 7.96 and 7.97 extend a polynomial-uniformly approximated Hecke eigensystem to one global continuous semisimple representation r : G_{E} → GL_{a}(ℚ_{ℓ}). To assemble UpperTheory.Gal.Lim.limWU4_of

and UpperTheory.Gal.Lim.limFinOdd_of (and to pass from their joint power-sum output to the crystalline Weil–Deligne comparison via UpperTheory.Gal.ClosedPhiFromClosedTrace.congPhi_holds), we must trans-fer four additional local properties from the approximating odd-rank seeds to this same global representation r: (i) unramifiedness and Frobenius characteristic polynomials at every usable split spherical place w ∤ℓ; (ii) the de Rham and crystalline properties at every controlled place w | ℓ; (iii) exact equality of the Hodge–Tate jump multisets at every induced embedding over w | ℓ; and (iv) exact equality of the crystalline Weil–Deligne Frobenius power sums under joint approximation.

Crucially, in the Lean source the p-adic Hodge closedness theorems GlobalTheory.LimitTop.closedAtL and UpperTheory.Gal.ClosedPhiFromClosedTrace.congPhi_holds do not rely on any unproved external p-adic Hodge closedness interface (in particular, neither BhattScholzeIntegral nor DeRhamPotSemistable is invoked as an external hypothesis). Instead, they are proved directly from the universally quantified lo-cal period-ring data (P, AI, T) (LocPrime, LocAinf, LocTied) by constructing a ℤ_{ℓ}-lattice tower cover of the matrix algebra of r, extracting linked Breuil–Kisin frames of uniform pole height, and transferring filtra-tion bounds, crystallinity, Sen/Hodge–Tate power sums, and crystalline Frobenius traces along the tower. We next review the Breuil–Kisin prism and frame formalism used to propagate the de Rham and crys-talline properties across a pulled-back lattice-tower cover. For any finite extension K/ℚ_{ℓ} inside ℚ_{ℓ} with residue field k of cardinality ℓ^{aK} and uniformizer π ∈𝒪_{K}, the source constructs a Breuil–Kisin datum BK K consisting of 𝔖 = W(k)[[u]] (with Frobenius φ_{𝔖} extending Witt Frobenius by u →→u^{ℓ}), an Eisenstein mini-mal polynomial E(u) ∈W(k)[u] of π over W(k)[1/ℓ] whose constant term is ℓ times a unit, a compatible system of ℓ-power roots π^{♭} ∈𝒪_{ℂ}^{♭}_{ℓ} of π, and a Frobenius-equivariant evaluation map ev : 𝔖 → A_{inf} = W(𝒪_{ℂ}^{♭}_{ℓ}) sending u →→[π^{♭}] such that ev(E) generates ker(θ : A_{inf} →𝒪_{ℂℓ}) (nonempty_bk_of_finExt). Write ev_{W} : 𝔖 →W(ℂ^{♭}_{ℓ}) for the composition of ev with the natural inclusion incl_{W} : A_{inf} ↪→W(ℂ^{♭}_{ℓ}), and let 𝒪_{ℰ} ⊂ W(ℂ_{ℓ}^{♭}) be the ℓ-adic completion of ev_{W} (𝔖)[1/ev_{W} (u)]. Choosing a compatible system ε ∈𝒪_{ℂ}^{♭}_{ℓ} of ℓ-power roots of unity with ε^{(1)} ̸= 1, the element τ = ([ε^{1/ℓ}] −1)η ∈A_{inf} (for a unit η ∈A^{×}_{inf} solving φ(η) = ωη where ev(E) = ωξ_{ε}) satisfies φ(τ) = ev(E) τ and φ(η)([ε] −1) = ωη([ε] −1) = ev(E) τ (exists_isPer).

For a continuous ℤ_{ℓ}-lattice representation ρ : G_{K} → GL_{d}(ℤ_{ℓ}) and a height bound N ≥ 0, a Breuil– Kisin preframe (Pre) of height N consists of T ∈ GL_{d}(W(ℂ^{♭}_{ℓ})) and A, A^{′} ∈ M_{d}(𝔖) such that AA^{′} = E^{2N}I_{d}, ev_{W} (E)^{N}φ_{W} (T) = T ev_{W} (A), and ρ(g) σ_{g}(T) = T for every g ∈G_{K} fixing π^{♭}. Proposition 7.102 (Breuil–Kisin frames on layers, tower limits, and transfer of de Rham and crystallinity). Let K, L_{0}/ℚ_{ℓ} be finite extensions in ℚ_{ℓ} such that every ℚ_{ℓ}-embedding K ↪→ℚ_{ℓ} lands in L_{0}, let (P, AI, T) be local period-ring data with compatible core C (Fits T C), let bk be a Breuil–Kisin datum for K with period τ, and let Cv be a lattice-tower cover of (L_{0}, r, Cl) for G_{K} in rank a ≥1. Assume that for every ρ_{1} ∈ Cl, every finite-extension model R of ρ_{1} over L ⊃ L_{0} is semistable (IsSst) with Hodge–Tate jump multisets mult_{V} (R, τ_{K}, n) = count_{n}(J(τ_{K})) for a fixed family of multisets J, and set N = max_{τ} ′_{, h∈J(τ} ′_{)} |h|.

1. Layer semistability, crystallinity, and filtration bounds. For every m ≥0, the rational layer represen-tation q_{Rep}(ρ^{′}_{m}) on ℚ^{d}_{ℓ}^{′m} is semistable, satisfies

and is crystalline whenever every ρ_{1} ∈ Cl is crystalline.

2. Uniform-height Breuil–Kisin frames on each layer. For every m ≥0, there exists a de Rham Breuil– Kisin frame F_{m} of uniform height N for ρ^{′}_{m}, which satisfies F_{m}.IsCr whenever q_{Rep}(ρ^{′}_{m}) is crystalline.

3. Limit-lattice Breuil–Kisin frame extraction. There exist a de Rham Breuil–Kisin frame F_{0} of height N for the limit lattice ρ and an integer r_{0} ≥ 0 such that for every n ≥ 0 there is m ≥ n with Link(bk, F_{0}.T, F_{m}.T, Π_{m}, n, r_{0}). Moreover, if F_{m}.IsCr holds for every m, then F_{0}.IsCr holds.

4. Recovery on the limit lattice and read model. The representation q_{Rep}(ρ) is de Rham, and is crystalline if F_{0}.IsCr holds. Consequently, every finite-extension model R of r over L ⊃L_{0} is de Rham, and is crystalline whenever every ρ_{1} ∈ Cl is crystalline.

Proposition 7.105 (Spherical power-sum operators, Frobenius indexing, and dense usable intersections). Let E be a CM field, Ω an algebraic closure of E, ℓ a prime, ι : ℚ_{ℓ}≃ℂ, a ≥1, and d ≥1 with ImQ(E, d) (so E contains a square root of −d).

1. Rational spherical power-sum operators (sphOps). Theorem 7.106 (Trace-limit transfer for definite unitary representations). Let Rk : ℕ → Prop, Ty, Gen, and Wt be as above.

1. (UpperTheory.Gal.Lim.limWU4_of) If SeedWU4(Rk, Ty, Gen, Wt) and CongUW4(Rk, Ty, Gen, Wt) hold, then LimWU4(Rk) holds.

2. (UpperTheory.Gal.Lim.limFinOdd_of) In particular, SeedFinOdd and CongFinOdd imply LimFinOdd = LimWU4(Odd).

Proof. Part (2) is the immediate specialization of (1) to Rk = Odd, Ty = TyEll, Gen = GenOf(DGen), and Wt = WtLac. To prove (1), fix (E, Ω, ℓ, ι, a, d, T, U, w_{0}, v^{′}) satisfying the hypotheses of LimWU4(Rk). By FieldOK(E, ℓ, d), every place w | ℓ is split in E/E^{+}. Apply CongUW4 to obtain local levels K_{w} fixing U off w_{0}, v^{′}, with K_{w}(w) = GL_{a}(𝒪_{Ew}) at every split spherical place w of U apart from w_{0}, v^{′}, together with the joint polynomial congruence family hcong.

Because U is an irreducible automorphic representation of the definite unitary group, the set S of split places where U is not spherical is finite (finite_not_sph); moreover, by conjugate-place transfer of Satake parameters (exists_satU_of_under_eq), a split place w is spherical for U if and only if ApartAll(S, w). Set W_{0} = {w : IsSplitAt(w), ℓ ∈/ w, ∃B, SatU(U, w, B)}. By Proposition 7.105(1)–(2), construct (J, O, x, fr, n) over W_{0} with rational-coefficient operators. By existence and uniqueness of the local component of U at every split place (exists_comp_and_unique), O determines a unique eigensystem θ : J →ℚ_{ℓ} for U (IsSysU). Note also that any automorphic U^{′} with level K_{w} off w_{0}, v^{′} and spherical at v^{′} is automatically spherical at every split place apart from w_{0} and S (hsphSeed: at places conjugate to v^{′} by exists_satU_of_under_eq, and elsewhere because K_{w}(w) = GL_{a}(𝒪_{Ew})).

For every finite set Y of places of E, invoke SeedWU4 at (U, S, Y ) to obtain a finite set Z_{0}(Y ) of usable places coprime to ℓ and apart from w_{0} and S, together with a choice function assigning to every admissible seed U^{′} a continuous semisimple representation rr(Y, U^{′}) : G_{E} → GL_{a}(ℚ_{ℓ}). Enlarge Z_{0}(Y ) and define the controlled ℓ-adic set by

Z_{s}(Y ) = Z_{0}(Y ) ∪{w ∈Y : IsSplitAt(w), ℓ∈/w, ∃B, SatU(U, w, B)},

W_{s}(Y ) = {w ∈Y : ℓ∈w, Apart(w, w_{0}), Apart(w, v^{′}), ∃B, SatU(U, w, B)}.

Applying hcong at ((Z_{s}(Y ), W_{s}(Y )) yields nonzero scalars) c_{Y} (w, n) ∈ ℂ^{×} and a joint polynomial ap-proximation of θ ⊕ ι^{−1}(c_{Y} (w, n) PowSatU(U, w, n))_{Ws(Y )×ℤ} by congruent triples (Y, U^{ ′}, θ^{′}) satisfying all seed hypotheses (Good): U^{′} is unramified off T, has level K_{w} off w_{0}, v^{′}, is spherical at v^{′}, satisfies SameWtOff(ι, w_{0}, v^{′}, U, U^{′}), Wt, Ty, Gen at all places in Z_{s}(Y ) ∪W_{s}(Y ), and has eigensystem θ^{′} for O. Let I be the set of all such triples i = (Y, U^{′}, θ^{′}) satisfying Good(Y, U^{′}, θ^{′}), and set ρ_{i} = rr(Y, U^{′}), η_{i} = θ^{′}, and D_{i} = {j ∈J : η_{i}(j) = Tr ρ_{i}(x_{j})}.

By hcong at Y = ∅ and rationality of O.f_{j} (which reduces to Proposition 7.100), all values θ(J) lie in a single finite extension L/ℚ_{ℓ}. Moreover, for every Y , restricting the joint approximation hpaJ to the left coordinate via approx_left gives PolyApprox(θ, η^{′′}{i ∈I : i.Y = Y }).

We next verify the Chebotarev density hypothesis: for every finite subset s ⊂I, x(∩_{i∈s}D_{i}) is dense in G_{E}. Each seed i ∈I comes with an open dense set V_{i} ⊂G_{E} and a finite exceptional set X_{i} of places on which Frobenii g ∈V_{i} at usable places w /∈X_{i} satisfy the seed characteristic-polynomial identity. The finite intersection V_{s} =∩_{i∈s}V_{i} is open and dense in G_{E}. By Proposition 7.105(3), the set of Frobenii at usable places coprime to ℓ and apart from S ∪∪_{i∈s}X_{i} is dense in G_{E}, so its intersection with the open dense set V_{s} is dense in G_{E}, and so is its image under the homeomorphism g →→g^{−1}. For every such Frobenius g ∈V_{s} over a place w, we have w ∈W_{0}, so Proposition 7.105(2) gives an index j ∈J with O.pl(j) = w, fr_{j} = g, n_{j} = 1, and hence x_{j} = g^{−1}. For every i ∈s, the seed characteristic-polynomial identity at (w, g) and the forward clause of frobOpsIdx yield η_{i}(j) = Tr ρ_{i}(x_{j}), i.e., j ∈D_{i}. Thus g^{−1}= x_{j} ∈x(∩_{i∈s}D_{i}), proving density.

Applying Proposition 7.96 (exists_trace_limit) to (J, I, x, θ, L, ρ, η, D) yields a single function t : G_{E} → L satisfying the extended linear trace inequality for every polynomial approximation of θ, and

Applying Proposition 7.97 (ex-ists_limit_rep) to t yields one global continuous semisimple representation r : G_{E} → GL_{a}(ℚ_{ℓ}) with Tr r = t. By Proposition 7.101(1), LinApprox(r, ρ^{′′}A) holds for every such subfamily A ⊂ I. We now check all three conclusions of LimWU4(Rk) for this same r, specializing in each case to the subfamily

1. Usable spherical places w ∤ℓ with SatU(U, w, B). Fix a prolongation valuation subring A ⊂Ω over w with inertia group I_{A}. Since w ∤ ℓ whereas w_{0}, v^{′} | ℓ, we have Apart(w, w_{0}) and Apart(w, v^{′}), and also w ∈ W_{0} and ApartAll(S, w). By hsphSeed, every i = (Y, U^{′}, θ^{′}) ∈ A_{w} has U^{′} spherical at w; since moreover w ∈Z_{s}({w}) and w ∈i.Y , ρ_{i} satisfies the seed’s exact Frobenius-eigenvalue clause FrobEig at w. In particular, ρ_{i}(s) = 1 for every inertia element s ∈I_{A} and every i ∈A_{w}; by

For every index j ∈J with O.pl(j) = w, the seed’s FrobEig at w and the forward clause of frobOpsIdx give j ∈D_{i} for all i ∈A_{w}; hence Tr r(x_{j}) = t(x_{j}) = θ(j) = ι^{−1}(O.z_{j}(σ)). The converse clause of Proposition 7.105(2) (hconv) then yields ι(charpoly(r(s^{−1}))) =∏_{b∈}algSat_{(a,qw,B)}(X −b) for every Frobenius s over w.

2. Controlled spherical places w | ℓ apart from w_{0}, v^{′}. Since every embedding τ : E ↪→ ℂ lies over a unique place u of E (overPl_unique: two distinct maximal ideals are coprime, contradicting the ultrametric triangle inequality for x + y = 1), the hypothesis SameWtOff(ι, w_{0}, v^{′}, U, U^{′}) on every i ∈A_{w} implies SameWtAt(ι, w, U, U^{′}). Moreover, every i ∈A_{w} has w ∈i.Y and ApartAll(S, w), so the seed supplies CrysDRU(U^{′}, ι, ρ_{i}, w). Because U admits archimedean weights at every embedding (exists_hasWeightAt_of_isAutRepU) and LinApprox(r, ρ^{′′}A_{w}) holds, Proposition 7.103(3) (crysDRU_of_linApprox applied to closedAtL) yields CrysDRU(U, ι, r, w).

3. Joint approximation of Weil–Deligne power sums at w | ℓ apart from w_{0}, v^{′}. Assume SatU(U, w, B), and fix period-ring data (P, AI, T_{per}, A_{v}, O^{′}, B_{w}) and a Weil element σ ∈W_{Ew}. Then w ∈W_{s}({w}). Choosing weights λ(τ_{0}) of U at each τ_{0} : E ↪→ℂ, set C_{w} = ρ^{′′}A_{w} and J(τ) = jumpsOf(λ(ι ∘τ)). For every i ∈ A_{w}, CrysDRU(U^{′}, ι, ρ_{i}, w) and SameWtAt(ι, w, U, U^{′}) guarantee that ρ_{i} is con-tinuous, locally crystalline at w, and has jumps J(τ) at every induced embedding τ. Because w ∈ W_{s}({w}), every i ∈ A_{w} also satisfies Gen at w, so the seed’s fourth clause supplies phiSum(WD_{w}(ρ_{i}), σ, n) = phiSum(satWD(a, B^{′}), σ, n) = PowSatU(U^{′}, w, − deg(σ)n) for all n ≥ 0. Applying Proposition 7.105(4) (joint) to hpaJ at Y = {w} with index map p_{n} = (w, − deg(σ)n) and nonzero unscaling factors u_{n} = ι^{−1}(c_{{w}}(w, − deg(σ)n))^{−1} yields the exact JointApprox statement of LimWU4(Rk).

Because all three clauses use the exact same global representation r, this proves LimWU4(Rk).
